description: US annual returns 1928 to 2025: S&P 500 with dividends, 10-year Treasury bond, 3-month Treasury bill, CPI-U inflation; simple annual rates as fractions
provenance: re-extracted on 2026-11-13 from histretSP.xlsx; the CSV reproduces the SHA-256 pinned by seams §8 D2 byte for byte

sources.title: Aswath Damodaran, Historical Returns on Stocks, Bonds and Bills: 1928-2025 (histretSP.xlsx)
sources.section: sheet 'Returns by year', header row 20, data rows 21 to 118
sources.note: Equal to the pinned SHA-256: the workbook has not changed since the design's retrieval on 2026-11-10.

sources.title: Aswath Damodaran, Historical Returns on Stocks, Bonds and Bills: 1928-2025 (histretSP.xls)
sources.section: the same workbook in the older format
sources.note: Equal to the pinned SHA-256. Not read: the build environment has no .xls reader; the .xlsx gives the pinned CSV.

extraction.format: %d,%.6f,%.6f,%.6f,%.6f; header year,stocks,bonds,bills,inflation; LF line endings; trailing newline
extraction.never: the sheet 'Nominal vs Real Data', whose bill column differs in 42 years and inflation column in 73 at six decimals (its 1966 inflation is 3.36%, against 3.4591% here)

definitions: From the workbook's sheet 'Explanations and FAQ': stocks = dividends plus price change of the S&P 500 over the start level; bonds = the coupon promised at the prior year-end 10-year yield plus the price change of a constant-maturity 10-year bond; bills = the average 3-month rate over the year; inflation = the change in the CPI for all urban consumers, not seasonally adjusted (FRED).
notes: The HTML page shows 17.78% for the 2025 S&P 500 return; the workbook holds 0.177237, which is used (seams §9 item 12).

The workbook is replaced every January. A new workbook is a data-version bump with new expected values in data.test.ts; if it cannot be re-extracted, the committed CSV stays and this file says 'extract of 2026-11-13, not re-fetched'.
